title: David's harp (1 Samuel 16:14–23)
hookLine: David plays and Saul's dark mood lifts

lines: THE KING IS IN THE DARK.
cards: One verse says the spirit of the LORD came on David. The very next says it left Saul. And something else comes instead.
The text calls it an evil spirit from the LORD, and it terrifies him. The king is in the dark, and his servants can see it.
So they suggest what people still suggest for someone who's low: let us look for a man who can play the harp. When the dark comes on you, he'll play with his hand, and you'll be well. Saul says yes.
Find me someone who plays well.

teach.h: A SON OF JESSE WHO CAN PLAY.
teach.b: One of the young men says: I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, skillful in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent, good-looking, and the LORD is with him.
So Saul sends to Jesse for David, who is with the sheep, and Jesse loads a donkey with bread, a skin of wine and a young goat, and sends his youngest son to the king.
Nothing in the text says Saul knows what happened in Bethlehem, where this boy was just anointed with oil among his brothers.

teach.h: THE RIVAL WALKS IN AS A HELPER.
teach.b: David walks into the palace not as a rival, but as a musician, to help the man whose throne he'll one day sit on.
And the text is tender: Saul loved him greatly, and David became his armor-bearer. Let David stay with me, Saul sends word, for he has found favor in my sight. The chapter ends with a picture.
Whenever the spirit from God was upon Saul, David took the harp and played with his hand, and Saul found relief, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.

teach.h: DAVID TOOK THE HARP, AND PLAYED WITH HIS HAND.
teach.b: The Hebrew word for this harp is kinnor, a stringed instrument. The book doesn't say what he played, or whether there were words. Just that someone played when the dark came, and the king was well.
This week, a boy said speak, a mother named what was lost, a people asked for a king, a king hid and then kept the showy offering, and a shepherd was chosen for his heart.
Today that shepherd sits down beside the king, and plays.

how: Jews read David's playing for Saul as part of the Former Prophets; by tradition, David is also linked with the book of Psalms.

o: a war trumpet blown to call Israel to battle
a gift of music Jesse sent the king with bread
the kinnor David played to lift Saul's dark spirit

games.q: David in the palace — tap the pairs.
p: find a man who can play
sent bread, wine and a young goat

s: Jesse sent David to the king empty-handed
he loaded a donkey with bread, a skin of wine and a young goat.
the text tells us exactly what song David played
it says only that he took the harp and played with his hand, and Saul was refreshed.
the text says Saul loved him greatly, and made him his armor-bearer.

games.q: you're one of Saul's servants. the king is tormented and terrified, and nothing seems to help. what do you suggest?
o: call the priests to offer a sacrifice.
find a man who plays the harp well, to play when the dark comes.
leave the king alone until it passes.
games.why: they suggest a harp player, and one of them already knows a son of Jesse. when David played, Saul was refreshed, and was well.

practice: Think of one person in a dark stretch right now, and one piece of music that might reach them: a song they love, a song from a better year, something quiet. Choose it, and hear a little of it in your head.
If you pray, hold that person before God while you listen.

wordCard.voice: David's harp. The kinnor the young shepherd played for Saul, so that when the dark came, the king was refreshed and well.

orig.note: Hebrew: kinnor, the stringed instrument David played for Saul.

carryVoice: Your line: music lifts. The rival walked in as a helper. A week in Samuel, done.
